highlights.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
highlights.summary: The exchange froze transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.
body: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week.
Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack, which is said to be the largest hack in history.

The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach, but that the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.

"Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," Binance posted on X.

highlights.title: Penguin Colony was made to 'put the games industry on notice'
highlights.summary: The latest game from Origanme Digital ( Umurangi Generation) reimagines H.P. Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness through the eyes of Antarctica's indigenous inhabitants, transforming a seemingly absurd premise into a deeply personal work of psychological horror.
body: At first glance, Penguin Colony might look like a cute, if slightly unsettling, throwback to the PlayStation 2 era. You play as a penguin waddling, sliding, and swimming through the shadowy Antarctic wilderness, following a mysterious light. But there are also Nazis. And ancient cosmic horrors. And a searing indictment of colonialism lurking beneath the ice.

In a sprawling conversation with Polygon, Faulkner unpacks how penguins, Nazis, Lovecraft, and his own Indigenous perspective collided to create a bold new lo-fi horror game that is also extremely playable. Below, the artist explains why he felt compelled to confront everything from the violence in Palestine and what he sees as a failure of the video game industry to respond to the horrors unfolding in plain sight, in a package where nailing the level design and core mechanics were just as important as the messages.

Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness through the eyes of Antarctica's indigenous inhabitants, transforming a seemingly absurd premise into a deeply personal work of psychological horror.

body: The next year, Wendig reported that he and Sykes had entered into a deal with Thomas Vitale ( Slasher, Pandora ), who co-wrote and co-produced a movie based on Wendig and Sykes' viral Twitter story, with Pandora ’s Brett Simmons attached as director. The result was 2018's You Might Be the Killer, a horror/comedy starring Fran Kranz ( The Cabin in the Woods ) and Alyson Hannigan ( How I Met Your Mother, Buffy the Vampire Slayer ), with a brief cameo by Keith David.

You Might Be the Killer debuted at 2018's Fantastic Fest in Texas, then made its way around the international festival circuit before being released directly to streaming via Shudder. As a result, YMBTK was already a little obscure for all but the most devoted horror fans... and then COVID hit, which relegated everything from before 2020 to a strange liminal before-time.

Sadat, now based in Germany, saw her latest feature “No Good Men” open the 76th Berlinale before screening in Tokyo. Film scholar and presenter Takasaki Ikuko moderated.

The session followed other reflections on women’s careers in film at the festival, both in its Women’s Empowerment section and at an animation symposium held earlier the same day on the past, present and future of four women working as directors in the anime industry.

The panel set out to discuss how women and feminism are presented in Sadat’s and Maksimović’s films and beyond, but it turned mostly to the practical, financial barriers standing in the way of more films directed by women.
Both filmmakers said getting the means to make a film often requires a certain conformity.

highlights.title: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
highlights.summary: Outsourcing planning to AI can lead people to surrender their own critical thinking, which can have potentially deadly results in places like the backcountry.
body: This story originally appeared on High Country News and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

By the time the three hikers called for help from a rocky face on Mount Shasta in Northern California, they’d made a series of bad decisions. They didn’t bring enough food, and they’d overestimated their fitness. Instead of turning back in late afternoon when they hadn’t yet reached the top, they summited at 7:30 pm and had to descend in the dark. Their lack of preparation and poor planning, as they admitted later, came partly from relying on Google’s artificial intelligence chatbot Gemini. By morning, they were lost on a gnarly part of the mountain, and one hiker had banged up his knee.

“We get plenty of people who come unprepared or don’t do any research at all. To these guys’ credit, they did try,” said Nick Meyers, US Forest Service program manager of the Mount Shasta Wilderness Climbing and Avalanche Center, which responded to the call. “But I think they kind of turned their brains off.”
points: Outsourcing planning to AI can lead people to surrender their own critical thinking, which can have potentially deadly results in places like the backcountry.

highlights.title: Clayface Comes in Second to You Can See Everything at the Domestic Box Office on Halloween Weekend
highlights.summary: Clayface has come in second at the domestic box office on the Halloween weekend as audiences continue to show up for Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything.
body: It was a narrow victory for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's comedic look into the life of the controversial Theranos creator, thanks to an estimated haul of $10.6 million to the DCU movie's $10.4 million (Note: These positions could change once final totals are tallied Monday). You Can See Everything's limited international rollout means Clayface is comfortably first globally ($22.8 million), but in what is technically the doc's third weekend in theaters, becoming the number one movie in the domestic market is still an impressive feat.

It's less of a warning of how audiences feel about Clayface and more of a sign that the behind-the-scenes peek at Holmes' life has real staying power. Originally released to just 855 theaters October 16, the Fielder doc has benefited from strong word-of-mouth and stellar reviews (IGN gave it a 10/10 ). Movie social media platform Letterboxd even pointed out that the project quickly emerged as its highest-rated feature film ever, with its first weekend in theaters landing it in second behind Street Fighter.

“People from MLB told me that I had great timing and was making the film at just the right moment with Ohtani’s success,” said Romer at a screening before the film’s official Japan premiere at Tokyo International Film Festival. “But it was just coincidence. highlights.title: 6 Google Maps features that work better on Android Auto vs. CarPlay
highlights.summary: You would think that Maps would be the same regardless of your phone's brand, but there are some differences between the Android Auto and CarPlay experiences.
body: I tested Google Maps on both systems in the same car, and Android Auto made several everyday navigation tasks noticeably easier.

Google Maps is available on both Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, but it's not the same experience — even when using the same app in the same car. I performed identical searches, route changes and simple navigation tasks back to back on both systems using the same infotainment screen.

Generally speaking, the fundamentals are close. Both provided me with a speedometer, lane guidance, incident reporting and alternative-route suggestions, as well as the standard controls for avoiding tolls, highways and ferries. The differences were much more apparent after I began using Maps for more than just getting from A to B.

The benefits of Android Auto range from minor interface details to features that still work better there than on Apple's offering. CarPlay does recover a few points, but Google Maps generally feels more at home on Google's own platform. Shocking, I know.

highlights.title: 5 Classic Nintendo Games That Are So Good They Never Need a Remake
highlights.summary: Video games have been around for so many decades that the next time you sit down to play one, you’ll have tens of thousands of terrific options to choose from. A lot of us find ourselves playing newer releases when the time rolls around, because older titles have slipped from our minds.
body: Some of those old games will feel rough, and may include mechanics or stage designs we find difficult to enjoy. Others hold up remarkably well, to the point where the most we might ask for is a slight resolution adjustment, or a few quality-of-life improvements. Otherwise, they’re nearly perfect. In case you’re looking for titles that fit that bill today, here are five classic Nintendo games so good they never need a remake. Just keep making them available wherever you can, Nintendo, because they’re fine exactly as they are.

The Super Nintendo launched alongside Super Mario World. The pack-in game was a revelation, designed to perfectly utilize a bunch of new hardware perks. Sprites scaled. Parallax scrolled. Players could tap a shoulder button to let Mario look ahead and see upcoming hazards before they were all up in his face. Colors were richer and more varied.

But even if you have a smart TV, you might not be taking full advantage of it. Fortunately, it's easy to add new apps to a Samsung smart TV if the ones you want aren't already included when you first set it up.

If you only need the most popular streaming services, you might not need to do anything to get them running. Samsung smart TVs usually come pre-loaded with the Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video and Apple TV apps, though that list can change depending on which apps are available in your particular region. For anything else ( like these free channels for your smart TV ), you'll have to download a new app from a built-in search feature on your TV. And after downloading those apps, you'll probably want to do some rearranging on your home screen.

highlights.title: Footage of what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked
highlights.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Persona tragics have been begging for remakes of the first two games in the series for ages (at least, the ones who aren't begging for remakes of the PS2-era Shin Megami Tensei games instead). After thoroughly milking Persona 4 and 5, series producer Kazuhisa Wada said in August, "personally, I think it's something we should definitely do."

Now, almost two minutes of footage from what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked via the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It shows some dungeon exploration, typically flashy combat, and a dialogue scene all in the modern Persona style.

Oddly, Tatsuya from Persona 2 is one of the party members, though it's possible this is a cross-promotional skin you can equip. Or maybe the remakes will incorporate some kind of Persona Q-style crossover?

While it's fair to be suspicious this could be AI-generated footage, it seems both a bit too long and too internally consistent for that to be the case. And it's not like Atlus hasn't got form, given that we found out the Persona 3 remake was real via a leak as well.

Along with it, five to seven minutes of legendary suffering only possible in the world of Clive Barker’s cinematic and literary nightmare.

Outside, art director Cam Carbia’s design sees the cursed, mechanical plot device flayed open, its “doorway” to hell speckled with embedded programmable LED lights, restrained by chains and ripped flesh. Inside, scenic designer Dylan Kollath constructed a disorienting labyrinth of pleasure and pain out of a big-screen world based on Barker’s novella The Hellbound Heart. “When we pitched to Clive, he was very adamant that this haunted house would feature both,” says Lora Sauls, Assistant Director, Entertainment, UOR. “He made sure that our teams didn’t take out the sexual layer of those films.”

highlights.title: Lymphatic Drainage: 4 Simple Habits to Add to Your Daily Routine
highlights.summary: From deep breathing to rebounding, experts explain the small daily habits that can help support healthy lymphatic flow—and why it matters beyond depuffing.
body: Lymphatic drainage has become something of a wellness obsession. From sculpting facial massages to body brushes and compression boots, there are seemingly endless ways to coax away puffiness and encourage a more contoured appearance. But the benefits of a healthy lymphatic system extend well beyond what we can see in the mirror.

The lymphatic system is sometimes described as the “Cinderella of medicine”: “underestimated, yet performing a large part of the essential work,” writes cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. Gerald M. Lemole in his book Lymph & Longevity: The Untapped Secret to Health. While its aesthetic benefits have helped bring lymphatic drainage into the mainstream, this intricate network of vessels, nodes, and fluid is fundamental to everything from immune function to maintaining the body's fluid balance.
And, as it turns out, keeping it functioning properly doesn’t necessarily require a standing appointment with your facialist.

Think of the lymphatic system as the body’s behind-the-scenes maintenance crew. Working alongside the circulatory and immune systems, it helps collect excess fluid from tissues, transports immune cells, and carries certain waste products away from cells.

highlights.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
highlights.summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts.
body: New research shared exclusively with Kernel Panic shows that hackers have started adding AI functionality into a new strain of infostealer malware, making it possible for the system to automatically profile victims and quickly surface the highest value targets and their information. Dubbed “Volta-Autodoxer” because of how the malware refers to itself internally, the finding by Cisco Talos researchers sheds light on the ways that commercial LLMs are being used to augment and enhance the capabilities of established types of malware.

“Volta is pretty mature as a stealer. It casts a pretty wide net for what it collects,” says Ryan Fetterman, a security researcher at Cisco Talos. “It compiles all of those things together, ultimately producing a serialized dossier that it can send to a couple LLM models. It’s asking the model to act like an intelligence analyst and produce structured citation-backed assessment of the victim. It’s like a prioritization and analysis function.”

Talos flagged the malware using its new CAIRN framework, built to identify hacking tools that incorporate AI capabilities. Fetterman notes that Talos did not track whether Volta has been used in the wild.

body: Antonelli became the youngest world champion at 20 years old in Mexico, sharing a podium with race winner Max Verstappen and second-placed Lewis Hamilton. He has taken the title in only his second year in the sport after a remarkable season including nine wins.

“It’s a special moment,” said Antonelli. “One that we’ll remember for ever.” While his race engineer, Peter Bonnington, suggested this may well be the first of many. “It’s a ­pleasure to be on the journey with you, but it’s just the first chapter,” he said.
The defending champion, Lando Norris, led what were fulsome ­tributes to the driver who had taken his crown, emphasising that he felt Antonelli had been exceptional.

“He’s done an insane job. I feel like people are not giving him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” said Norris. “He’s beaten the teammate that’s been in the sport for four times longer than him. Who was also very good and who took the battle to Lewis Hamilton.”

highlights.title: Jakarta World Cinema Plans to Revive First Feature Competition With International Jury
highlights.summary: Jakarta World Cinema aims to bring back its First Feature Competition next year, open to filmmakers from around the world and judged by an international jury. This year’s edition did not accept submissions.
body: Next year, the team wants to bring in international jury members with strong filmographies, so the category can open to submissions from filmmakers worldwide.

The festival sits between October’s Jakarta Film Week and the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival at the end of November. Its lineup is made up of “80-90% award-winning films from Cannes, Berlin, Venice and Sundance,” according to Frederica, executive director of Jakarta World Cinema and director of KlikFilm, who oversees acquisitions.
“We travel to [different] film markets, Berlin, Toronto, Cannes, etc.,” says Frederica, adding that the festival aims to bring the year’s most important art films to local audiences.

This year’s edition has 102 theatrical titles, the most in the festival’s history, out of a total program of 207. Programming director Daniel Irawan says the goal for next year is to expand the lineup and keep working with its main venue, CGV Grand Indonesia, to increase audience capacity.

highlights.title: Forget maxxing your life. 2027 must be the year we relax – and start minning | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile. Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, minning means doing them less, if at all. Public service announcement: fellow citizens, we have maxxmaxxinged.
body: Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile – surely nobody who ever set out to funmaxx achieved it (see: New Year’s Eve), not even Dua Lipa. Minning is much more noble: it’s about making the world, rather than only yourself, better. Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, it means doing them less, if at all.

Back in the days when all of this was fields and we only used one x in “max”, it was clear that max volume is too loud, max capacity too crowded, and max power too draining. Somewhere along the way we lost sight of that. Let’s take a deep breath, and enjoy the relief of leaning into minning. First person to suggest they’re doing maxxminning will be taken to the tower and made an example of.
